Instead of allowing these historic artifacts to remain forgotten, our project transforms scientific information into an engaging digital experience. Visitors can explore different spacecraft, rovers, and scientific instruments, discover their missions and achievements, and learn where they were left behind. Through interactive maps, timelines, and storytelling, the website makes space exploration history easier and more enjoyable to understand, especially for younger generations. details:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive educational website designed to bring attention to the spacecraft, rovers, and scientific equipment left behind by NASA missions on the Moon and Mars.

 

The project addresses the challenge of making the history and significance of these abandoned artifacts more accessible and engaging, especially for younger generations. Our website organizes scientific and historical information into an interactive experience, allowing users to explore different artifacts, learn about their missions and achievements, discover their locations through interactive maps, and follow the history of space exploration through timelines and storytelling.

 

The website includes several sections, such as an artifact collection, interactive maps, a timeline, and educational stories. These features help transform scattered scientific information into an organized and engaging learning experience.

 

The main benefits of the project are preserving the historical legacy of space missions, increasing public awareness of space exploration, and making scientific knowledge easier to understand and access.

 

Our creative approach is combining scientific research with storytelling and interactive digital features. Instead of presenting the abandoned equipment as simple historical objects, we give each artifact an opportunity to tell its story and explain its importance.

 

The project was developed as a web-based solution and published online using GitHub Pages. It relies on digital information, research, and interactive website features rather than physical hardware.

 

Our goal is to make these forgotten artifacts remembered, understood, and appreciated as an important part of humanity's journey into space.
